nodes.label: email-client CLI (email-client + email-client-send + daemon)
nodes.rationale: Provider-agnostic IMAP/SMTP across any number of accounts, each with its own credential, watermark, and notification stream; provider auto-detected from the email domain. Preferred over the google skill for everyday Gmail because it needs no Google Cloud project.

nodes.label: Email Poll Daemon (IDLE push + poll fallback)
nodes.rationale: One worker per watched (account, folder) holding a persistent IMAP connection; IDLE-capable servers push in real time and polling (default 15s) is the fallback cadence, not the primary mechanism. The watch set recomputes live so adding accounts or folders needs no restart. Deliberate stop/restart never fires daemon_died; only an unexpected death does.

nodes.label: Email Standing Rules Section (trigger → action)
nodes.rationale: Durable user rules are recorded one per line as [account|all] when <trigger> → <action> so they map cleanly onto mark/move/draft/notify commands; one-off instructions are never recorded.

nodes.label: Email Delayed Send + Undo
nodes.rationale: Sends wait 30s by default as one persisted client-wide setting, not a per-send option. Only the poll daemon dispatches queued mail, so email-client-send refuses to queue while the daemon is stopped. A message cut off mid-dispatch may already have reached the server, so read Sent before undoing or resending.

nodes.label: EMAIL_DRAFT_ONLY Draft-Only Mode (email-client)
nodes.rationale: A CLI-level safety guarantee, not a behavioral promise: send/reply/forward are refused before touching SMTP while --draft and --dry-run still work. Guards email sending only; calendar writes with attendees are a real outward send it does not cover.

nodes.label: email-client Calendar Commands (CalDAV)
nodes.rationale: Event ids are iCalendar UIDs naming the whole series, so update/delete/respond affect every occurrence; single-occurrence cancels use delete --occurrence. Attendee emails ride the server's implicit scheduling (RFC 6638): the skill writes the event and the provider does the emailing. Microsoft accounts have no CalDAV and point to the microsoft skill.
